canonical_statement: The review aimed to compare nintedanib with pirfenidone for progressive pulmonary fibrosis using FVC change and mortality.
The review also aimed to compare pooled antifibrotic efficacy between IPF and progressive non-IPF fibrosis using FVC change and mortality.
The primary analysis outcome was change in forced vital capacity (FVC).

outcome.definition: Change in FVC; standardized when needed to combine absolute and percent-predicted metrics.

canonical_statement: The secondary analysis outcome was total all-cause deaths during the included study periods.

outcome.definition: Total deaths occurring during each included trial period.

canonical_statement: The investigators conducted a PRISMA-aligned systematic review and meta-analysis registered in PROSPERO as CRD42021266046.
MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for antifibrotic trials, with database searching spanning 1990 through the end of July 2021.
Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials in adults with lung disease using pirfenidone or nintedanib and reporting trial results suitable for FVC or mortality extraction.

population.label: Eligible adult randomized trial populations
inclusion_criteria: Trial results with extractable FVC change or mortality

canonical_statement: Studies were excluded when an English-language full text was unavailable or when the work used animal or laboratory models.

Two investigators independently reviewed abstracts and extracted study design, antifibrotic type, duration, sample size, FVC change, and all-cause mortality; disagreements were adjudicated by a third investigator.
Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized controlled trials by two investigators with third-party adjudication.

Random-effects meta-analyses pooled standardized FVC change and all-cause mortality; heterogeneity used Cochran Q, sensitivity used leave-one-out analysis, and publication bias was assessed by funnel plots.

The final review included 11 papers representing 13 randomized controlled trials; all 13 contributed FVC data and 11 had mortality data, reduced to 9 mortality analysis units after pooling paired INPULSIS and CAPACITY trials.

population.label: Included evidence set: 11 papers / 13 randomized controlled trials

canonical_statement: For FVC analyses, IPF trials included 2,872 participants (1,564 active treatment) and non-IPF trials included 1,292 participants (647 active treatment); the 13 trials comprised 9 IPF and 4 non-IPF trials.

population.label: FVC meta-analysis populations: IPF and non-IPF progressive fibrosis

canonical_statement: Three included studies had some risk-of-bias concerns in one domain: Maher 2020 for selective reporting, Behr 2021 for missing outcome data/imputation, and Azuma 2005 for selective reporting; the remaining studies were rated low risk across domains.
In IPF nintedanib studies, about 21% of participants received prednisolone up to 15 mg/day, while concomitant prednisolone use was minimal overall in the major pirfenidone IPF studies.

Anti-inflammatory therapy varied substantially in the non-IPF studies; the authors reported frequencies ranging roughly 5% to 63% across study populations and could not isolate its effect in most trials.
Across all 13 trials, antifibrotic therapy reduced standardized FVC decline versus control with a pooled standardized mean difference of -0.306 (95% CI -0.371 to -0.241; p<0.001).

population.label: All IPF and non-IPF trials contributing FVC data

canonical_statement: For the overall FVC meta-analysis, Cochran Q was 13.9 with 12 degrees of freedom (p=0.306), providing no statistically significant evidence of heterogeneity.

population.label: All IPF and non-IPF trials contributing FVC data

concept.text: Between-study heterogeneity of standardized FVC treatment effects

canonical_statement: Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis produced pooled FVC effect sizes ranging from -0.286 to -0.328, indicating little change in the overall estimate.
The funnel plot did not show evidence of publication bias for the standardized FVC analysis.
In IPF studies, antifibrotic therapy reduced standardized FVC decline versus control with a pooled effect of -0.305 (95% CI -0.389 to -0.222; p<0.001).
In non-IPF studies, antifibrotic therapy reduced standardized FVC decline versus control with a pooled effect of -0.307 (95% CI -0.431 to -0.183; p<0.001).
The IPF-versus-non-IPF subgroup difference in standardized FVC treatment effect was not significant (Q=0.001, df=1, p=0.979).

concept.text: Difference between IPF and non-IPF pooled FVC treatment effects

canonical_statement: Across nintedanib studies, the pooled standardized FVC treatment effect was -0.340 (95% CI -0.442 to -0.238; p<0.001).
Across pirfenidone studies, the pooled standardized FVC treatment effect was -0.266 (95% CI -0.355 to -0.178; p<0.001).
The pooled FVC effect did not differ significantly between nintedanib and pirfenidone studies (Q=1.139, df=1, p=0.286).

concept.text: Difference between drug-specific pooled FVC treatment effects

canonical_statement: Across the 9 mortality analysis units, antifibrotic therapy reduced all-cause mortality versus control (risk ratio 0.701, 95% CI 0.539 to 0.911; p=0.008).

population.label: IPF and non-IPF studies with mortality data

canonical_statement: For the pooled mortality analysis, Cochran Q was 5.613 with 8 degrees of freedom (p=0.69), showing no evidence of heterogeneity.

population.label: IPF and non-IPF studies with mortality data

concept.text: Between-study heterogeneity of mortality treatment effects

canonical_statement: Among IPF studies, antifibrotic therapy was associated with lower all-cause mortality (risk ratio 0.637, 95% CI 0.469 to 0.866; p=0.004).
Among non-IPF studies, all-cause mortality was not significantly reduced (risk ratio 0.908, 95% CI 0.547 to 1.508; p=0.71).
The non-IPF evidence included more participants receiving nintedanib than pirfenidone (494 versus 153), so non-IPF conclusions were considered more secure for nintedanib.
FVC was reported in both absolute and percent-predicted metrics, requiring standardized differences that reduce the intuitive clinical interpretability of the pooled effect size.
Different approaches to imputing missing FVC data across trials complicated interpretation of absolute effect magnitude.
Mortality was analyzed as binomial death events because hazard ratios were not consistently available, rather than using time-to-event meta-analysis.
The review focused on FVC and all-cause mortality because exacerbation and quality-of-life outcomes were not consistently reported or measured comparably across trials.

The authors concluded that antifibrotic therapy protects against FVC decline with similar pooled efficacy for nintedanib and pirfenidone and no obvious difference between IPF and progressive non-IPF fibrosis.
The authors concluded that larger controlled non-IPF studies are required before a general mortality benefit from antifibrotic therapy can be established.
The article reported no funding.
The authors declared no conflicts of interest.
The article stated that data and materials availability was not applicable.
